newsitem.title: USA: Bush believes he treated White House "with respect".
newsitem.headline: Bush believes he treated White House "with respect".

text.p: Former President George Bush hopes he will be remembered as having treated the White House with respect.

"I hope it can be said that we did it with honour and that we treated the White House with respect," Bush said during a fundraising appearance for St. John's Northwestern Military Academy in Milwaukee's western suburbs Thursday night.
The 72-year-old former chief executive did not elaborate or make any direct reference to the fund-raising controversy that has engulfed President Clinton, to whom he lost in 1992.
Asked what his legacy would be, Bush said "I don't know. I think we'll let history make that determination."
He received the academy's annual American Hero Award and reviewed high-school age cadets as they performed a full dress march.
"It means a lot to me when you see that parade, see a bunch of young guys whose lives have been shaped with a military background and training as part of it," added Bush, a Second World War veteran.
